Subject: RE: Redwood demo + procurement next steps

Samantha — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Really appreciate the thoughtful questions from your infra and ML teams. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so procurement has what they need to move quickly: 

Summary / ask from GreenGrid: 
- Goal: Move from POC to production inference for forecast pipeline (initially ~200 reqs/min, spike to 1k/min).
- Timeline: Ideally procurement kickoff in early April, target contract signature by end of month.

Next steps (what I'll send by EOD):
1) Draft SOW for POC + production readiness (attached: Redwood-SOW-draft.pdf)
2) Pricing summary showing hosted vs dedicated vs private, and the committed vs on-demand options (I'll follow up with a short spreadsheet)
3) Callout of procurement items: accepted payment methods (PO vs card), standard term sheet / redline process, SOC 2 and audit artifacts.

Procurement questions for you (to confirm):
- Primary procurement contact and email for legal/PO processing?
- Do you require purchase orders for all vendors, or only above a threshold (e.g., $50k)?
- Any marketplace preference (AWS Marketplace, GCP Marketplace) for ordering?

Recommendation (from an initial product fit perspective):
- For POC: hosted API (on-demand) to iterate quickly and avoid infra commitments.
- For production with predictable throughput: Dedicated (reserved capacity) with 12-month commit tends to get the best unit economics and predictable latency/SLOs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) is available if you need strict network isolation or regulatory controls — we can scope separately.

Please confirm procurement contact and whether GreenGrid prefers PO or card so I can tailor the SOW and pricing sheet. If useful, we can do a 30-minute procurement sync next week.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Marissa Cole

Samantha/Tom — thanks for the fast response and the procurement context. Quick answers below and attached a short pricing summary.

Answers to procurement items:
- Payment methods: We support PO and corporate card. We typically process POs via our finance team for orders over your PO threshold; for card payments we'll provide standard invoicing.
- Marketplace: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace (pricing and commit options vary by procurement flow). We can provide a marketplace ordering path if GreenGrid prefers that route.
- Compliance: attaching SOC 2 summary and links in the pricing sheet. Full SOC 2 Type II report can be shared under NDA.

Pricing / packaging notes (high level):
- Hosted (on-demand): Lowest friction for POC. Billed per token/request, no upfront commit. Good for short trials and fast iteration, but unit cost is higher at scale.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Predictable latency and lower per-unit cost for sustained throughput. Typical commercial path: 12-month commit with monthly invoices. We can offer commit discounts and onboarding credits for standard deals.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): For regulated environments or strict network controls. Usually priced via a platform license + hosting OPEX.

Attached: pricing-summary.xlsx (CSV-friendly) — it includes sample numbers for (a) hosted on-demand, (b) dedicated 12-month commit (baseline + discount tiers), and (c) private deployment ballpark.

For the procurement call on 2027-04-07, Rishi (cc'd) can join to discuss commercial terms and commit options; Aditya/Dev can join for technical procurement questions (SOC2, network). If it helps, I can also prepare two proposed commercial tracks: 
  1) Quick path: Hosted POC paid by card, then move to Dedicated commit once production readiness is proven.
  2) Faster production path: 12-month Dedicated commit with an initial POC clause and a PO-based billing cadence.

Please confirm: (1) time for 4/7 call, (2) whether GreenGrid wants the AWS Marketplace route, and (3) any specific legal items to pre-seed in the SOW/term sheet.

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Fwd: Redwood pricing — GreenGrid procurement path

Looping in a short internal note after reviewing the thread and attachments. Recommended commercial packaging to present on the 4/7 procurement call: 

1) Default recommendation: 12-month Dedicated reserve with a 30-40% commit discount, plus 1 month free (or credits) for onboarding — this aligns with GreenGrid's predictable usage and finance preference for PO.

2) Hybrid path for procurement flexibility: Host the initial 30-day POC on Hosted on-demand (card) to de-risk. Include an option in the SOW to convert POC usage into committed capacity within 30 days of POC completion; that allows them to start quickly while preserving a PO-based invoice flow for the committed spend.

3) Marketplace / procurement notes: If GreenGrid uses AWS Marketplace, confirm whether they expect Marketplace charges for the committed discount; sometimes committed pricing is handled off-marketplace which requires PO and invoice-based billing. We should prepare both a marketplace SKU and an off-marketplace invoice option.

Action items for Marissa: 
- Confirm whether Tom will accept AWS Marketplace purchase for committed offers or needs off-marketplace PO.
- If off-marketplace, get Tom's PO template and billing contact.
- I'll draft a short commercial offer doc with pricing tiers and invoice examples for both flows.

I'll have a draft commercial offer by EOD 4/06; Rishi, can you review the discount tiers quickly?

Thanks —
Aditya
